(OST) as a key harm reduction strategy to prevent

treatment of PWID with opioid dependence with 
a long-acting opioid agonist medication for a 
prolonged duration of time through the sublingual 
route, in a dose which effectively minimizes craving 
and withdrawals, and thereby enables the patient 
to stop injecting drugs and regain a stable life.

Combined with psycho-social interventions, the 
OST program has proved to be relatively successful 
in reducing drug related harms including HIV/HCV 
transmission and opioid overdose.

Evidence has 
also shown that early enrolment in OST programs 
remains a key factor in the reduction of new HIV 
infections among intravenous drug users, increases 
adherence on ART and improvement in the overall 
quality of life for the PWIDs.

application may vary from one jurisdiction to another, its essence remains consistent: once a court has rendered a final judgment on a case, that same 
matter cannot be re-litigated between the same parties.

In essence, res judicata signifies the irrevocable resolution and conclusion of a legal dispute by a 
competent court.

This principle serves to prevent the repetitive litigation of identical issues, thereby fostering certainty and conclusiveness within the 
legal system.
